title: A question suddenly occurred to me
author: Amiya_desi
selftext: Right now, you can usually only identify AI-generated games by their visuals and music; as for the code, there’s really no way to know without decompiling it. But if someone uses AI to generate initial game assets—and then manually redraws and rearranges the music based on the best results from the AI's output—would that still count as an AI game?

comments.body: bro, just polish your game and it's good. AI is a tool. lots of professionals stopped writing code manually months ago.

comments.author: unfamily_friendly
comments.body:
Have you heard about vegans? They don't eat meat, they don't drink milk, they don't wear leather, they don't use shampoo tested on anymals, some are strictly againt having pets.

With this in mind, there's two parts of AI art. Quality part is, AI art is very generic and boring, and human art has a big variety. Redrawing the faces and hands in your style and/or drawing after AI generated concept - this makes the final image much better. Issue solved, quality improved, no one would ever spot AI

The ethical part is, anti AI will hate it anyway. If you heavily edit AI picture, or redraw the AI concept by hand, or use it for inspiration, or if your product is 100% made manually, but anime girl on your PFP is AI generated - the digital vegans will bully you for it.

comments.author: ChirpXel
comments.body:
Well in steams terms to avoid the "Made with AI" tag, no actually. It is NOT considered AI-generated anymore.   
  
But you must make a significant amount of change from the AI generated content for it to be considered human made instead.

comments.author: Hot_Professional8287
comments.body: Yes, it would still count as an AI-assisted game, but that's where the industry needs to go. AI belongs UNDER the hood. Once people start frequently delivering polished, AI-assisted games, then the stigma is going to go away. It'll become a general quality check like anything else.
